items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: So lately, I've played the Money Tree with Gerald and Herb Jeffries

ctx.x: with Tatum, who was also a pretty decent piano player. So lately, I've played the Money Tree with Gerald and Herb Jeffries, and then we played another one at the Holiday Inn up in Ventura, and also we played a couple of weddings here and there and a couple of parties -- and I've just been really enjoying myself more than I can explain, really. You see, when Gerald and I work together, Gerald just... He doesn't have to call the tunes. There's some kind of signals. I couldn't begin to explain them. But he just…

Because that's the way I thought Duke Ellington used to start his band off. He would strike a note and never say a word, then all of a sudden he would bring his hand down, and the band would shower, and it was always a mystery to me how they knew what was going on. But now I think I understand, after having worked with Gerald. When you work with anybody for a long period of time, and you get so used to what's going on until certain sounds suggest certain things.
